Out of the smoke at the back of the rout came a woman's voice. It wasn't a horn or a captain. It was hoarse and cracked past music and enormous, the voice of someone who had learned to be heard across a playground forty years ago and had never needed to use it since.

She stood on a slab of fallen masonry in the exact center of the collapsing army. She wore no mask and no crown and had no bodyguard. Ravenia Caliphas was thirty meters away fighting to reach her and would not make it in time. The Queen of Ambria stood alone above the heads of the rout, holding a sword she had not cleaned in six hours.
She was not shouting commands. She was shouting names.

"Caliphas, left, take the left! Dacia. Dacia the Third, I know your name. I saw you at Castor with a broken arm. You did not go to the rear then either. Get up! Knife Company! Serrano's company, Serrano's dead, that makes it yours, so take it! You told me to my face three days ago that you were not my subjects. Prove it. Prove it here and prove it now. Hold with me!"

"For nine years I've been wrong. You can spend the last minutes of the world proving I was right about you, or you can spend them running. I don't care much which. But you will not do it where I can see you."
Here and there, in ones and twos across a hundred meters of collapsing ground, people stopped.

The party added their own names to hers: the witches and clan folk who had held the green sector, the two rangers they had pulled out of the drowned valley, anyone they had ever stood beside. Then the ones and twos became tens, and the line started to exist again where seconds before there had only been a crowd.

title: The Deep Trolls
description: Agathara's returning light has just cleared the eastern approach when the flagstones jump. A section of paving forty feet across stands up on one edge like a lid coming off. The trolls who climb out from the deep dark under Symbar are not forest trolls. They are the old kind, grey and slab-bodied, and they come up in total silence.
searchHint: flagstones stand up like a lid, deep trolls rise from under Symbar, thirty, complete silence, sapper laughing
narrativeSource: Book Three — I Am the Bill (2026-08-10)
narrative: Where the gap had been there was a sudden silence. The flagstones in the middle of the eastern approach jumped about a foot in the air. Then they did it again.

Then a section of paving forty feet across stood up on one edge like a lid coming off a pot. Something reached out from underneath and pushed it the rest of the way over onto the things standing beyond it.
They came up out of the deep dark under Symbar the way water comes up a well shaft.

They were trolls, but not the ragged forest kind. They were the old kind, the deep kind: grey, slab-bodied, mossed over with a thousand years underground. The first one had to turn sideways to get a shoulder out of the hole. Then it stood up, to a height that made the Ambrians nearest it simply sit down.
There were thirty of them, and they did not shout.

That was what everyone remembered afterward. The whole square was screaming, and the trolls came up in complete silence and looked around and worked out which way was which. Then they walked into the back of the host that had just broken through, without ever breaking into a run, and it came apart in front of them like wet paper.
One of them picked up something the size of a horse and threw it two hundred feet.
Somewhere on the wall an Ambrian sapper who had been fighting for eleven hours started laughing and could not stop, and had to be sat down.

title: Apple Blossoms
description: Aluin looks up at the World Serpent without any fear at all. "Oh," he says, "that's what it is." Then he says goodbye to his family and throws himself into the sky. For a while nothing changes. Then beams of green and white light begin to spear out through the serpent, and apple blossoms come down.
searchHint: Aluin dives into Uron, green and white beams of light, apple blossoms, the serpent dissolves into a blizzard of blossoms
narrative: They found each other again in the smoke, winded and scattered. Agathara had screamed until she had no air left to scream with. Out of the fog came Little Bear, and beside him was Aluin, looking up at the thing in the sky.
He was not even slightly afraid.
"Oh," he said. "That's what it is."
He looked at it for a while longer, and they watched him work it out. There was nothing else on that square big enough for it. Nothing else in the world, maybe.
"Well," said Aluin, "I guess I have something that I'm big enough for."
He turned to them. "You've been my friends and my family. And you saved me. And now I guess it's my turn to try to save you."

He squared his shoulders and drew the great sword, and he launched himself into the sky. A five-and-a-half-foot boy with a five-foot sword flew at a serpent two hundred feet across. Then he was gone into it.
Agathara had her hand up, reaching after him. Don't go. Aro had to pull her back into motion.
For a solid minute nothing changed. The serpent did what it was doing. The fighting went on and the running went on.

Then a beam of light speared out through its side, green and white, solid at the core and fraying at the edges. Then another, and another, all over the vast body, as if a tree made of light were growing inside the thing and coming out through its skin. At the ends of the beams the light came apart into apple blossoms, and they began to fall across the square.

Everyone stopped and looked up. The whole mountain of the creature came apart into blossoms: a tower of pink and white petals the height of the sky, collapsing and blowing outward across Symbar like a blizzard. Nobody could see anything. The whole square smelled of apple blossom.

title: Sidriana Rises
description: Two terrified Queen's Rangers left a talking urn in the Azure Palace and would not go near it again. Reginald translates the gold inlay: Sidriana. They pour out a sample. The black tar inside will not stop coming, and it rises into the shape of a woman who has been dead for a thousand years.
searchHint: urn of Sidriana, black tar spills, spirit rises, Azure Palace, Queen's Rangers Edvid Almin
narrative: The Rangers, Edvid and Almin, had found the urn in a tower bedroom and carried it down before they realized what it was doing, and since then they had refused to touch it. It talked, they said. Not out loud.

It was black ceramic, about a meter tall, with gold inlay that Reginald could almost read. One name was clear: Sidriana. That was the name on the tablecloth in the records room, the founder who had led her people to this valley. The rest were words for holding, binding and keeping.
Inside was a swirling black substance like tar. A small sample seemed reasonable. Karano tipped the urn.
It did not stop.

The black poured out in a thick, gleaming flood that would not be stoppered, with no end to it, like the sorcerer's apprentice's buckets. It spread across the polished floor of the blue palace. Reginald backed away from it with his hands up. Then it stopped spreading and started to rise.

It drew itself up into a figure: a tall woman made of oil and shadow, long hair falling down her back, every fold of an old-fashioned robe picked out in gleaming black. She turned her head and looked at them, and they heard her inside their minds without any sound.
Aro's sense for danger, which had never once failed them, stayed completely quiet.

She was not angry. She was grieving. She had been sealed in a jar while her city drowned, and the mud had dried, and now strangers were standing in her palace. The Rangers were pressed against the doorway in pure terror.
"She's a very sad old spirit," Agathara told them kindly, "not a demon lady."

title: A Tree Grown Through Him
description: In the witches' grove, where corruption stops at the edge of the spring grass, they offer Reginald a way out. They bite a leather stick between his teeth and open him with a knife. Then they grow a tree up through his body to drink the corruption out of him.
searchHint: witches cleanse Reginald, tree grown through organs, Blight Mark removed, leather stick, Amnar
narrative: The grove was a perfect circle of spring in a dead forest. There was green grass and there were flowers, and for the first time in seventeen days they heard a bird. Crossing the boundary was like stepping out of smoke. The corruption stopped at the edge of the grass.
The witches gave them everything they had left: healing potions, arrows, antidotes, spores, elixirs. It was the last resupply any of them would get before the end, and everyone knew it.
Then the witch Amnar looked at Reginald's hands.

He had lived at the edge of his own corruption for months. He was Blight Marked, the stigmata black to the wrist, one bad day from becoming something that would have to be put down. There was a way, she said. It would hurt.
They laid him on a table of living wood. They put a leather stick between his teeth and he bit down on it. Amnar opened him with a knife.

She pressed a seed into the wound, and it grew. A pale sapling came up out of his chest, its roots threading through him, and its branches went black as they rose. The tree was drinking the corruption out of him, and he felt every inch of it. He arched off the table and screamed into the leather, and the witches in their bark masks held him down and kept singing.
When the tree had nothing left to take, it withered, and they pulled it out of him root by root.

He lay there afterward looking at his hands. The black was fading off them. His Blight Mark was gone. He felt cleaner than he had in months, younger, and he could not stop turning his clean hands over in front of his face.

title: The Ring-Bearer
description: A towering winter elf declares the Iron Pact over. The covenant is broken, she says, and the darkness of Davokar has opened its eyes. Karano asks her for the Iron Pact ring anyway, and she gives it to him.
searchHint: winter elf grants Iron Pact ring, Karano ring-bearer, the Iron Pact is over, darkness of Davokar opened its eyes
narrativeSource: Book Three — The Hall of a Thousand Tears (2026-02-11)
narrative: She was taller than any of them, taller even than Karava. She had feline features, pale armor, and two slender artifact swords at her hips. Karava, who did not get nervous, got quiet.
She was not hostile. She was resigned, which was worse.

"The time of the Iron Pact is over," she said. The darkness of Davokar had just opened its eyes. The elves were closing the Hall and taking down its portals so its power could not fall to what was coming. They would keep three gates open in the south for human refugees. The Prince had gone to Symbar, stubborn as a fool, to defend the one who sang under the tree.
Karano was of the Pact. He had walked these halls before. He spoke Elvish, and hearing it from the eternity elf at the door had moved him more than he had let anyone see.
He asked her for the ring.
She looked at him a long time. The covenant was broken, she said. There was nothing left for a ring to mean.
He asked anyway.
"We forged these," she said at last. "Do as you wish." She took the iron band and put it on his arm herself, and the oldest order in Davokar had one more sworn member on the day it ended.
"I'll fight the darkness," Karano said, "to my dying breath." She had heard many oaths in her life, and from her face she believed this one.
Then she lifted the body of Mayor Nightpitch from beside the well, carried it away into the dark, and did not come back.

title: Across the Black Water
description: A fifteen-meter stream of liquid corruption cuts across the dead forest, and swimming it would kill Reginald. They spend a whole day felling a tree to bridge it. When Reginald slips on the log, Karano has him by the wrist.
searchHint: Blackwater stream of liquid corruption, felling a tree to bridge it, Karano anchors rope, hauls Reginald back
narrative: The stream was the color of wet slate and moved like oil. It came up from somewhere underneath the world. Its banks had withered back for yards on either side, and corrupted beetles fed at its edges and grew fat. Moths with screaming faces on their wings drifted over it.
Swimming it would cost more corruption than Reginald had room for. A raft would cost less. A bridge would cost least of all.

There was a dead tree that would reach. Felling it was harder than it looked. Reginald and Agathara swung at it and failed, comically, and cracked an axe handle doing it. Karano did the rest. When it came down it splashed black corruption over all of them.
He crossed first, light on his feet, and tied off a rope on the far bank so the others would have a line to hold.
Agathara went over like a dancer and did not seem to notice the drop.
Reginald was halfway across when his boot slid. One moment he was walking the log and the next he was going over sideways toward the black water with nothing in reach.

Karano already had him. He had come back out onto the log without anyone seeing him move, and his hand was locked around Reginald's wrist. He had one foot braced and the other hand on the rope, and the scholar hung over the stream from his grip.
He pulled Reginald up as if lifting a pack. Neither of them said anything. On the far bank they cut the rope and left it there.

title: The First Standard Falls
description: Losadra's three iron standards have killed every connection to Prios in Saroklaw Square. Karano has worked out that they are what has to fall. He puts armor-piercing shot after shot into one of them until it bends and splits, and for Agathara it feels like a break in the clouds.
searchHint: iron standards, corrupted sanctifying rite, Karano armor-piercing arrows breaks a standard, Agathara feels the cloud cover break
narrative: The standards were longer than a man and solid iron, driven into the flagstones by runners from Losadra's column. While they stood, nothing holy worked properly in the square. Agathara fought on crippled. Aro was a guttering outline that could not land a blow. Every sun token on every soldier's chest had gone cold.
Karano shot Ervano Vearra's sword hand first and set it on fire, because he could. Then he looked at the standards again and understood that they were the real target.
Arrows did not like them. Most of his shots pinged off and shattered against the iron. The things were ringed with flesh-reaper imps, small hook-boned creatures that had once been people.

He switched to armor-piercing heads and worked one standard the way he would work a stubborn lock, putting every shot in the same place. On the fourth one the iron took a visible bend. He put the next shot into the bend.
The standard split. A chunk of it went spinning away across the flagstones, ringing.

Across the square Agathara felt it like clouds breaking in the rain, a flash of sunlight through the overcast. Her power did not come back all the way, but some of it came back. The shield around each of her companions brightened visibly, all at once.
Everybody understood what that meant. The standards were how this would be won.
Karano nocked another arrow and looked for the next one.

title: Over Her Broken Body
description: Agathara has fallen thirty feet onto a corrupted ledge and her leg is broken. Armored beetles the size of dogs crawl out of the black fungus to swarm her. Aro stands over her and none of them gets past him.
searchHint: Agathara shattered leg 2 HP, Chasm Stag beetles, Aro Master Bodyguard, screaming beetle siren, cliff ledge
narrative: She had not been able to slow her fall. She came down the washed-out cliff stair onto the ledge and her leg folded the wrong way beneath her. The sound it made was enough. She lay where she had landed, white-faced and bleeding, with almost nothing left in her.
The ledge was crusted with black fungus, fat and bubbling with sludge, and out of it came beetles.

They were the size of foxes and armored, and they spread out to flank like wolves. They had acid in their bites. Their shells, when cracked, released poison. They went for the woman who could not get up.
Aro came down the cliff in one controlled drop and landed over her.

He did not leave her side for the rest of the fight. He stood astride her with his sword moving, and every beetle that came for her met the blade first. One bite still got past him and burned acid into her broken leg. That was the only one.
Then one of the beetles stopped fighting, threw back its head, and began to scream.

It was not a sound of pain. It was a call, a siren meant to tear the air open and summon something worse through it. Karano's arrow went down its open throat and it burst. Reginald kicked another one off the ledge before it could burst on top of them.

Aro fumbled once. The poison found him through the gaps in his light, his focus slipped, and for two terrible breaths he was barely there at all. Then he was solid again, still standing over her, and the beetles were dead or gone.
Below the ledge, something larger was stirring.

title: The Dead Elves' Road
description: Aeon Iroh unmakes the living and has a monster for everyone who makes a noise. The elves who walked it before them left a trail scratched into its walls. Aro, who does not need to fear the dust, finds the first mark.
searchHint: dead elf gatherers' glyphs, not the open ways, go down by the embalmers, find the broken butterfly, Aro spots the first marker
narrative: The city ran to every horizon, grey with dust under a violet sky that was not a sky. Something the size of a building passed overhead now and then, blotting out the light, and smashed into some distant part of the ruins with a sound like a landslide.
Every half hour the city took a little more from the living. Aro was already dead, and it did not trouble him.

He walked ahead of the others along the edges of the alleys, looking at the walls. The elves had spent a thousand years mapping this place one gatherer at a time, each walking as far as they could and scratching what they had learned for the next. Someone had to have left a sign.
He found it low on a wall where the dust had banked up against it. He knelt and brushed the grit away with his golden fingers, and the scratches came up in his light.
Not the open ways. The open ways are watched. Go down by the embalmers, under-streets where the dust lies still.

There were more marks after that, in alley after alley, each one scratched by a different hand. Don't make light. Don't make sound. Don't climb too high. And at last, in a hand that looked very tired: Find the broken butterfly.
They went down by the embalmers, where the dust lay still. They did not talk. When they had to signal one another, they tossed a little dust.

title: The Valley Drowned
description: Sidriana takes them into her memory. They see the founding of her city and her people's cheering, and her kneeling before the giant with six wagons of tribute. Then they see its end. Symbar drags the crown ship over the mountains, and from the Throne of Thorns he breaks the peaks and drowns the valley.
searchHint: Sidriana's vision, Emba Silba founding, Garavax pact, Simbar drags the crown ship, Throne of Thorns shatters the peaks, flood
narrative: She did not tell them. She showed them. The vision was complete in every sense: they smelled it and heard it and felt the cold of the mountain air.

Refugees came over the mountains into a green valley. A woman with silvery-grey hair, in a fur-lined azure cloak, climbed a boulder above them and spread her arms. "Welcome home," said Sidriana, "to the cradle of enlightenment, to Emba Silba." The cheering went on and on. The city rose in what felt like an afternoon, built to keep out the darkness and the corruption.

They saw her kneel before the Lord of the Cliff with six wagons of slaughtered game behind her. It was tribute for peace. The giant would be feared and appeased and never defeated, and for a long time that was enough.
Then they saw the end.

A king rose from an overgrown throne on a dais carried by motionless warriors. Behind him, dragged over the mountains by more people than they could count, came the stone ship with the crown, the same ship they had seen beached in Symbar.
That was the first time they saw the Throne of Thorns in action.

The peaks at both mouths of the valley broke off and fell, and the people were trapped. The rivers rose at his command, the water came down on the city, and his army in double ranks cut down everyone who ran.
The vision ended in a blinding flash from the colonnade temple. Several of them were bleeding when they came back to themselves, from the skin, from wounds no weapon had made. Sidriana was weeping.

title: The Queen Unmasked
description: Two sisters who have not spoken in years face each other across Saroklaw Square, and nobody will speak first. Frank, in immaculate linen, walks out alone and opens the parley. Then the Queen of Ambria does something nobody has seen in thirty years. She takes off her mask.
searchHint: parlay at Saroklaw Square, Frank opens the parley, manual of etiquette, Korinthia removes her mask, Stand with me then judge me after
narrative: They came into the square by different roads and arranged themselves with enormous care. Ambrian infantry stood to the south in ordered blocks. The undead stood to the north, and they did not shift. The witches stood in a loose crescent to the west, and the last twenty-four of the Thorn Pack in a line across the east. A bier under cloth-of-gold was carried in by six slaves and set down at the edge of the square, and both armies pretended not to look at it.
Nobody would speak first. The silence stretched and went sour.
Agathara leaned over to Frank. He had crossed Davokar alone in clean linen to bring Reginald lunch at the end of the world. She asked if he would get things started.

"Pardon?" It was explained to him. "I see. We do seem to be at a bit of an impasse. Perhaps let us now consult the manual of etiquette in this situation." He visibly turned the pages of a book in his head. "Yes. That will do, I believe."

He walked alone into the middle of Saroklaw Square. "Ladies and gentlemen, we have been gathered here today for a parlay. Korinthia, my lady, you are the head of the largest state left in existence, and therefore you hold the floor."
The Queen looked at him for a long moment. "Franklin, you have been a joy and a delight the whole time I've known you. Carry on, good sir."
Then she reached up and took off her mask.
Nobody had seen her do it in thirty-odd years. She was older than anyone expected, and a scar ran across her face from the war and her captivity. She never spoke in public. She spoke now.

"I came here for a chair. I spent nine years, forty thousand lives, and my sister, and my mother's rest, on that chair. And it is broken. I'm not going to stand here and ask you to trust me. You would be fools to do so. I ask you to stand with me for the next couple of days. Stand with me, and then judge me after."

title: The Forest Stands Up
description: For a thousand years the black root cover over Symbar lay perfectly still. At dawn on the last day it is moving the way a lake moves in the wind. Then, with no signal, it opens across two-thirds of the city at once, like skin peeling back, and everything that was buried under it walks out.
searchHint: dawn, root cover opens like skin peeling back, thousand years of buried things, walking thorn-trees, the dead, ninety seconds to the wall
narrative: Nobody slept, and everybody pretended to. Fires burned every twenty yards along the wall, because whatever came would come up in the dark.
At dawn they saw it plainly: four miles of Davokar, and none of it was acting like a forest anymore.

The root cover had lain over Symbar like a black skin for a thousand years, and through all of those years it had been still. That was the thing about it that made the hair stand up the first time anyone saw it. Now it moved the way a lake moves in a light wind, a slow restlessness miles wide. Every few seconds a patch of it bulged, held, and sank back. They had watched enough by now to know that the ones that did not sink back were the ones that opened.

A smell came off it that nobody could name. The oldest barbarian on the wall, a woman of seventy with red flower dye still on her face, said her grandmother had a word for it. The word meant the air in a grave when you first break it open. She would not say it aloud. You did not talk about such things where they could hear you.
There was no signal and no horn.
Across two-thirds of Symbar, in the same second, the root cover opened. It did not open like a door. It peeled back like skin.

Out of it came things that had been under it since before Ambria existed: pale and jointed, with limbs bent wrong, blinking at a light they had not needed in a thousand years. Thorn-things four meters high, which had been trees an hour before, walked and dragged their own roots behind them like torn skirts. Behind them, in a slow grey tide that did not hurry, came the dead: a thousand years of Symbar's dead, and every corpse the roots had taken since.
It was ninety seconds to the wall. From the deck of the Crown Ship a woman's voice carried across the whole square.
"All sectors, nobody chase them. Hold!"

title: I Am the Bill
description: Sister Losadra has stood for nine hours in the middle of her army, raising every coalition soldier who falls near her. When the party comes for her she makes a single gesture. Two thousand flesh-crafted step back and open a ring of empty flagstones sixty feet across. She plants her black sword and waits for them.
searchHint: Losadra opens a sixty-foot circle, plants her black sword, you unmade the world with clean hands, I am the bill
narrativeSource: Book Three — I Am the Bill (2026-08-10)
narrative: She had spent the whole fight on the north side. For nine hours she had stood in the middle of her own army, and every time one of the coalition's soldiers fell anywhere near her she reached out with one gauntleted hand in an unhurried little gesture and they got back up. There were Ambrians in her ranks now. There were witches. A Beast Clan warrior with red flower dye on his face stood at her shoulder with his own axe still in his back.
She was not fighting the battle. She was harvesting it.
Agathara's beam of light washed over her and split and peeled away, and she paused. She turned her head and looked at them.
Then she did the last thing they expected. She sent everyone away.

It took one gesture. Two thousand flesh-crafted things stepped back and opened a circle of empty flagstones sixty feet across in the middle of the worst battle in the history of the world. She stood in the center of it, planted the black sword point-down in the stone, leaned on it and waited. The noise of the apocalypse went on all around a perfect ring of silence.

"Now it's just us," said Sister Losadra. "Do you know how long I've been dead? Do you know what it's like to be dead and awake for it? Two years, every hour of it, and every hour I spent thinking about the three of you, and about a street in Ravenia, and about the fact that I was right."

"I said you were a rot. I said it when it was unfashionable, when the Curia was going soft and the Duke was making pets of heretics and everyone wanted to be kind. I said they'll pull it all down. And here we are. There's no Ravenia. There's no Thistle Hold. There's no Ambria. There's no church. The throne of a thousand years is broken. You did all of that, not me. All I ever did was burn villages."
"You unmade the world, and you did it with clean hands, and you've never once been made to look at the bill."
She lifted her sword and came across the ring toward them.
"I am the bill. And it's time to be paid."

title: Who You'd Leave the World For
description: They wake among the roots of the Mother Tree after the escape from Aeon Iroh. Aluin is sitting by himself with his greatsword across his knees, trying to work out what he has become. Agathara sits down beside him and waits for him to speak, and by the end of it the two of them are family.
searchHint: Aluin what am I now, family, sister, Mother Tree roots, greatsword across his knees
narrative: They woke between two roots, each wider than a city street, in a nest of moss that someone had laid around them with care. Ten hours had passed. The woods were silent: no birds, no insects, nothing in the branches of the greatest tree in the world. The only sound was something very large shifting in its sleep far below them, felt more in the teeth than heard.
Aluin was outside, leaning against a root with his greatsword across his knees and his fingers tapping on the blade. He was staring at nothing.
Agathara sat down next to him and didn't say anything. He started to speak twice and stopped.
"I've known you since I was little," he said finally. "I was little and you were so big, and then I got big, and then you got little, and now I just feel so little again."

It came out of him in pieces. He had spent his whole life being part of creation, and the biggest thing that had ever happened to him was watching a world come apart. "And I loved it. And I had to go to it. And I wanted to go to it." He looked at her. "What am I now?"
"You get to choose," she said.

He asked how she had chosen. She thought about it honestly. "I think I knew more what I didn't want to be. And I knew what I wanted to fix. And I figured out how to become the person who could fix the things that were wrong."

There was more under it, and it came out too. He missed his father. His mother was not herself; the forest was eating at her. He did not know who he had left. "That's why when I saw you guys there, I had to save you instead of go to the world."
Agathara bumped his shoulder with hers. "Isn't that what family is? Who you would leave the whole world behind to save?"
He thought about that for a while. Then he said he had always wanted a sister, and she said she had always wanted a punk little brother. He smiled for the first time since they had come home.

title: The Mirror
description: Losadra has hunted them for two years. Now she has run Reginald through and stands over him. Agathara has had enough. She takes out the little silver hand mirror with roses on its back, and a single line of Prios's light cuts the Whip of Prios in half from crown to heel.
searchHint: Sister Losadra killed, rose-inlaid hand mirror, Prios Burning Glass, cut in half, Reginald down with a sword through him
narrativeSource: Book Three — I Am the Bill (2026-08-10)
narrative: The last iron standard had gone down in a spray of steel, and Agathara's power had come back so bright that it was like a stadium's lamps all coming on at once with her at the center. That had been an hour and a lifetime ago.
Then Losadra had sent her army back and opened a ring of empty flagstones sixty feet across in the middle of the worst battle in the history of the world, and planted her black sword, and waited.

Nobody in that ring had come out of the fight clean. Aro had taken a stroke meant for Agathara, and in the shock of it he had cut his own leg off with his backswing. Karano had rolled his ankle, gone down on his back, and kept shooting from the ground. Reginald had needled through her plate from behind until her armor's retribution threw him across the stones, bleeding and black with corruption. Agathara had healed him, and he had gotten up and gone back in.

The whole time, Agathara had kept talking at her. Did you think I was just going to lie down and die while you hunted me? You made it all this way and you can't even hit me. How pathetic. She had kept Losadra's attention on her, and kept her away from the others.
Losadra's last swing went into Reginald instead. He fell in front of Agathara with the black sword through him, and the dead woman looked straight at her.
"That's one more for the record books."
Agathara knelt and brushed Reginald's hair back from his forehead, and the healing went into him. Then she stood up.

She was done. Losadra had tried to ruin her life. She had tried to make Agathara afraid and to make her run. She had dug up her own dead and walked them across half of Davokar to make Agathara look at them.
From the pocket of her robe Agathara took a small silver hand mirror with roses inlaid in its back. She tilted the glass toward Losadra.
The light that came out of it was a single line. It started at the crown of Losadra's head and went down to her heels, and it did not stop on the way.

Losadra went to her knees in two pieces that hadn't yet understood they were apart. "Prios," she was saying. "Prios dictates my faith, and it condemns you. It always did. It always— It's so very cold. Why is it so—"

Every crow in Symbar left at once. It was the loudest single sound of the whole day: thousands of them rising off the ruins and the standards and the dead in one enormous dry roar, a black smear going north and growing smaller. The light came back to Saroklaw Square the way it comes back into a room when someone opens the shutters.

title: Through a Drawn Sword
description: In the Queen's pavilion, Reginald tells Korinthia that the power node is gone. She orders that no one who knows it leaves the tent alive, and her Field Marshal draws and comes at them. Reginald doesn't step back. He tells her that it wasn't the worst news he had.
searchHint: Korinthia's pavilion, no one leaves this tent, Ravenia Caliphas draws sword, Reginald keeps talking, root cover stood up
narrative: The Ambrian camp was everything a camp should be. The latrines were downwind and the horses properly picketed, and the sentries challenged correctly and apologized when they asked for weapons. The party handed theirs over. Past the wizard tents and the panzer alchemists dicing on their sapper kits, past a field hospital much too large and very full, stood the command pavilion.

Field Marshal Ravenia Caliphas never took her hand off her sword. The general looked them over the way a man looks at timber. Adelia Erobel of the Ordo Magica stood a little apart from both of them. Seated at the center, in a blood-red dress and a blank porcelain mask, the Queen of Ambria did not greet them, did not offer a seat, and did not move for a long time.
"There are two kinds of people in Davokar," she said at last. "Those who serve the light, and those who serve the dark. And the second kind lie about it. Which are you?"
They swore to the light. She thanked them and dismissed them to the ranks.
"We have big news," said Reginald. "It's kind of pressing."
He told her the cleanest true version he could. They had gone to the yonder world and seen the power node destroyed. Shock read straight through a blank mask. Ravenia's knuckles whitened on her hilt.
"What we say here must never be repeated outside this tent," said Korinthia. "General. No one leaves this tent that knows this."
The general moved. Ravenia's sword came out of its scabbard, and she came across the carpet at them with the point leading.
Reginald did not step back. He did not raise a hand. He kept talking, in the same reasonable voice, to the masked woman behind the blade.
"See, the trouble with that is that you're going to need all the fighters you can get. Because that wasn't the worst news I had to share."
There was a pause. "Wait," said the Queen. "Just a second. Continue."

He continued. He was halfway through explaining what the Throne's power had been holding asleep under Davokar when the ground rolled under the camp. A horse screamed somewhere and a tent pole snapped. A scout came through the flap white-faced.
"A mile of the northern root cover just stood up."

title: Every Language He Knows
description: The square is coming apart in slabs, and worms the size of river barges are bursting up under the formations to swallow whole squads. The Ambrian trumpets sound the retreat, but only the Ambrians know what the call means. Karano climbs the highest masonry he can find and roars it in every language he knows: get to the ship.
searchHint: sinkholes, spawn of Uron worms, fall back to the Crown Ship, Karano shouts in every language, fighting retreat
narrative: Losadra was dead and it had changed nothing. Then the ground started taking people.

The flagstones of Saroklaw Square came up in slabs, tilting like ice on a thawing river. Sinkholes opened fifteen and twenty feet across and swallowed whatever was standing on them. Something the size of a river barge burst up through the middle of a Beast Clan reserve, opened, took a hundred people into itself whole, and went back down. The flagstones settled over the hole. Someone counted nine of the things on the square, and from the sound of the rest of Symbar there were hundreds.

The plan was the ship. If everyone could get off the ground and onto the Crown Ship's deck, the worms couldn't come up under them. Korinthia had already given the order. Ambrian trumpets were sounding the retreat across the whole field.

Only the Ambrians knew what the trumpets meant. Karano watched the blocks of trained infantry fall back toward the center. Everyone else, the barbarians and the witches and the clan folk and the elves, kept fighting where they stood.
He found the highest slab of fallen masonry he could reach and climbed it.

Then he started shouting. He shouted in Ambrian, in Elvish, in the clan tongues, in every language he had ever learned a word of. To the ship. Get to the ship. If we're on board, we won't have to worry about the things beneath our feet.

When a worm came up under a knot of fleeing soldiers, he did not try to kill it. He shot it in the face to make it flinch, again and again, buying them the seconds to run. Then he went back to shouting.
